name: Insecure Credentials
summary: Adversaries may target insecure credentials as a means to persist on a system or device or move laterally from one system or device to another. Insecure credentials may appear as default credentials which are pre-configured credentials on a system, device, or software that are well-known in documentation or hard-coded credentials which are built into the system, device, or software that cannot be changed or not easily changed because of the…

analytics.name: Analytic 2048
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies successful authentication to Windows-hosted Industrial Control System (ICS) applications using credentials matching known default or hardcoded vendor passwords. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.

analytics.name: Analytic 2203
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies authentication attempts against Industrial Control System (ICS) network device management interfaces using default or hardcoded vendor credentials from sources not in the approved Network Management System (NMS) Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) subnet. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.

analytics.name: Analytic 2219
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies successful authentication to an Industrial Control System (ICS) device or application using credentials that are either documented vendor defaults (T1694.001) or extracted from configuration files/firmware where stored in cleartext (T1694.002), from a source not in the approved access list. This technique-level analytic unifies both sub-techniques.
